players.product: X-ray metrology for 3D transistor & advanced-packaging process control (with Onto AI Diffract)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jun Kawakami: 2Q FY2026 consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY (up 20% QoQ after a 1Q transition period), driven by Semiconductor Process Control Instruments; gross profit margin was essentially flat YoY (higher costs offset by higher selling prices and a better customer / product mix) and operating profit was below the prior year as planned strategic investments continued (operating margin bridge from 14.3% to 9%). Semiconductor Process Control Instruments 2Q revenue grew 60% YoY and operating profit 70%, with revenue up significantly in both memory and logic; Multipurpose Analytical Instruments revenue had not yet returned to growth but recovered to a level close to last year; Services revenue grew 11% on price increases and more maintenance contracts, while EUV mirror, handheld Raman analyzer and preclinical imaging revenue shifted into 2H. For 1H, revenue decreased approximately 3% YoY, with Semiconductor Process Control Instruments revenue up 18%.
quarterly_data.figure: 2Q revenue +7% YoY, +20% QoQ; semiconductor 2Q revenue +60%, operating profit +70%; Services +11%; operating margin 14.3% to 9%; 1H revenue approximately -3%, semiconductor 1H revenue +18%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: company-wide 2Q orders increased by more than 50% YoY and 1H orders by more than 25%; the pipeline of opportunities expected over the next 12 months has increased by more than approximately 35% YoY. Semiconductor Process Control Instruments 2Q orders rose to more than three times the year-earlier level and 1H orders grew 86%, supported by memory production increases and the recovery in demand from North American IDMs, with order levels very strong heading into 3Q and 4Q. Multipurpose Analytical Instruments orders grew 5% in 1Q and 6% in 2Q (Japan +22% on power semiconductor and electronic component customers; US +50%, including a large XRTmicron order in the power semiconductor field), while a considerable amount of European orders shifted into 3Q; the 3Q order outlook for this category is expected to exceed 50% YoY growth, with Asia and China forecast at around 20%. The company developed LablincStudio, a software platform to integrate its instruments into customers' automated, AI-driven materials-discovery systems.
quarterly_data.figure: 2Q orders +50%+ YoY; 1H orders +25%+; 12-month pipeline +35%+; semiconductor orders more than three times in 2Q, +86% in 1H; Multipurpose Analytical Instruments orders +5% (1Q), +6% (2Q), 3Q outlook over +50%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the FY2026 outlook: guidance is left unchanged for the time being. The initial guidance was approximately 9% underlying revenue growth company-wide (approximately 4% for Multipurpose Analytical Instruments and approximately 21% for Semiconductor Process Control Instruments); the Multipurpose recovery has been slower than planned, but semiconductors have clearly stronger momentum than planned and should offset the shortfall, and management believes there may be some upside to revenue; an upward revision of overall guidance could be possible if visibility into the profit margin improves, which it does not yet have. In Q&A he said 2H requires more than JPY60 billion of revenue with around 60% gross margin, that semiconductor growth is expected to be considerably higher than assumed at the beginning of the year (whether it reaches 30% is another matter), that semiconductor visibility for this year's revenue is quite high, and that the company would like to aim for 3Q revenue higher than 2Q, with 4Q still very large. Middle East uncertainties have had little impact so far.
quarterly_data.figure: Initial guidance: approximately 9% underlying revenue growth (approximately 4% Multipurpose, approximately 21% semiconductor); 2H needs more than JPY60 billion revenue at around 60% gross margin

quarterly_data.signal: CEO / Senior EVP Kiyoshi Ogata on new semiconductor products: of the approximately JPY14 billion of full-year FY2026 new-product revenue planned at the beginning of the year, approximately JPY4 billion was recorded in 1H (mainly XTRAIA XD and XTRAIA CD (T-SAXS)); management believes the full year will come close to JPY14 billion, implying approximately JPY10 billion in 2H (mainly XTRAIA XD, MF-3400, ONYX and XTRAIA CD (T-SAXS)), which it expects to contribute significantly to 2H margin improvement. Joint Evaluation Programs (JEPs): 14 were under way last year (five completed, nine carried over); five new JEPs started in 1H FY2026 so 14 are currently under way, eight of them scheduled to be completed this year, and the total this year is expected to probably exceed last year's. JEPs involve new high-end products with higher average selling prices; current capacity-expansion orders are primarily for the existing MF GEN3 (copy-exactly), while GEN4 (MF-3400) will be purchased for next-generation processes from 2H.
quarterly_data.figure: New-product revenue plan approximately JPY14 billion (approximately JPY4 billion in 1H, approximately JPY10 billion expected in 2H); 14 JEPs under way, eight to complete this year

quarterly_data.signal: Senior EVP Kiyoshi Ogata on the next-generation semiconductor roadmap (target: more than 50% share of a USD1 billion SAM by 2030; progress on track): the logic tool is still under development, with orders and shipments planned to begin next year (proof-of-concept work at the NanoTerasu soft X-ray beamline). XTRAIA XD (Si/SiGe metrology) has delivered 12 units cumulatively, JEPs are completed with four logic and memory manufacturers, it has begun to be applied in mass production and multiple-unit deliveries to individual customers have begun; it is also used for memory, including development of high-speed transistors for HBM. XTRAIA MF-3400 (GEN4, ultra-thin films such as high-k/metal gate) has begun shipping with adoption by major logic and memory manufacturers starting this year. ONYX3200 (ultra-thin aluminium films) is under evaluation at three logic and two memory manufacturers. A 300-mm in-line fab version of XRTmicron for stress / dislocation analysis of 3D DRAM multilayer SiGe films has begun deliveries. Asked from which memory generation its 3D structure shape metrology would apply, Ogata said adoption is already beginning, so it applies to the current generation.
quarterly_data.figure: Target more than 50% of a USD1 billion SAM by 2030; XTRAIA XD 12 units delivered, JEPs completed at four manufacturers; ONYX3200 in evaluation at three logic and two memory manufacturers

quarterly_data.signal: Senior EVP Kiyoshi Ogata on advanced packaging: Rigaku is developing a beta system for TSV void inspection and plans to deliver it to a customer by the end of this year; based on its evaluations to date the company says it is currently the only instrument capable of inspecting voids in extremely fine TSVs such as those used in HBM, and customers are evaluating it. Inspection (defect inspection) is a new area and Rigaku's first X-ray imaging technology developed for inspection, so its share target in this market was set conservatively at 30%, though he said the company can aim for a higher share.
quarterly_data.figure: Beta TSV void inspection system delivery to a customer by end of 2026; advanced-packaging inspection share target 30% (conservative)

quarterly_data.signal: Management on demand and position: citing a research firm, Ogata said Rigaku further increased its leading share of the X-ray metrology equipment market to nearly 40% in 2025 and became the number one player in the broader thin-film thickness and composition metrology market (including optical tools) in 2025. Kawakami said memory will grow very significantly in the FY2026 semiconductor revenue mix, with logic also above plan; Ogata said capacity-expansion investment demand at memory customers is very strong, particularly HBM- and DRAM-related, many new fab projects are still being planned and additional new demand is expected from next year. Rigaku has Rigaku Technology Centers in Silicon Valley and Taiwan and plans to open RTC-China in Shanghai by the end of this year.

players.product: Advanced-packaging inspection/metrology (Dragonfly G5, 3DI) + JetStep panel-level lithography

connects_to.relationship: Joint X-ray process-control solutions (Onto AI Diffract software + Rigaku X-ray metrology)

contracts.signal: Rigaku (Ogata / Kawakami): XTRAIA CD (T-SAXS) for deep-hole memory metrology has begun shipping with Onto's model-based software installed; concrete hybrid metrology plans with Onto have begun - the two companies will jointly develop step one and step two, working toward shipments of the first-step product as early as 2H this year or around next year, and are also jointly developing software for GI-SAXS (logic 3D structure shape metrology). Kawakami said the capital and business alliance with Onto was progressing as planned, with the transaction expected to close relatively early in 2H, after which full-scale hybrid metrology solutions are expected to expand rapidly.
